chunks: Kirdīn al-Mismaʿī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the bustard.
So he said: “I wish that I had some of it, so that I might eat until I am full.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abā ʿAbdillāh, a title of Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.أَمْتَلِئَ: I become full; emphasizing plentiful eating
key_terms.الْحُبَارَى: the bustard bird being asked about
key_terms.فَآكُلُ: so that I may eat; indicating consumption as food
key_terms.كِرْدِينٌ: Kirdīn, the narrator who asked the Imam
key_terms.لَوَدِدْتُ: I would wish; an expression showing approval or desirability

ai.seo_question: Is the ḥubārā bird halal to eat according to the hadith of Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that when Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about the ḥubārā bird, he expressed a desire to eat it. The wording indicates its permissibility as food and serves as evidence in discussions of halal hunting and slaughtering.
